summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman was admitted with acute chest pain and dyspnea that began suddenly at rest and worsened the following day. She had risk factors including diabetes, hypertension, and light smoking. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with negative cardiac enzymes and a normal ECG. A V/Q scan excluded pulmonary embolism, and an exercise MIBI stress test showed normal perfusion and good exercise tolerance. Wheezing was noted on exam, and she responded well to bronchodilator therapy, with complete resolution of chest pain. Her symptoms were attributed to reactive airways, possibly triggered by a recent URI. Chronic conditions including diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and obstructive sleep apnea were monitored and remained stable. She was discharged home on her baseline medications with an albuterol inhaler for as-needed use and plans for outpatient pulmonary function testing.
